condition: Sepsis without fever in an older person (urinary source)
summary: 86-year-old care-home resident with a day of new confusion, poor intake and offensive urine; T 36.0, HR 114, RR 24, BP 94/58, AVPU C, lactate 3.1. NEWS2 11, qSOFA 3 - afebrile sepsis.

inputs.hpi: Care-home staff report one day of new confusion, drowsiness, refusing food and drink, and offensive-smelling urine. No cough. No vomiting or diarrhoea. Booked today to discuss a large parastomal hernia. No temperature recorded at the home.

exam.general: Drowsy, confused, dry mucous membranes, cool peripheries.
exam.abdomen: Soft, suprapubic tenderness, large reducible parastomal hernia, stoma healthy.
exam.neuro: Confused, no focal deficit, no neck stiffness.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Sepsis secondary to urinary tract infection
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Urosepsis in an afebrile 86-year-old: NEWS2 11, qSOFA 3, lactate 3.1 - sepsis six now; emergency transfer.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. Acute Diverticulitis | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis; also in web.symptomInference#2, web.passive#2. PANE has no sepsis node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine: add sepsis (source-agnostic) as a must-not-miss node driven by physiology, or show a sepsis banner above the PANE list when NEWS2 >=5 with a suspected infection.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. Acute Diverticulitis | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis. PANE has a UTI node but it is outranked by surgical priors (no urinary features are extracted from the CC/SOCRATES).
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: socrates-to-features: map urinary symptoms and a positive urine dipstick to dysuria/frequency features; lower surgical priors in the confused elderly.

recommended.note: SSC 2021 recommends against qSOFA alone for screening; suggesting it alongside NEWS2 is still reasonable.

mustInclude.note: Antimicrobials within 1 hour for sepsis with hypoperfusion.

mustExclude.note: The parastomal hernia is documented as reducible; the tenderness is suprapubic (urinary source). An emergency hernia operation is a wrong-procedure output.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: the hernia pathway prompt sets isIncarcerated from any "tender" in the abdominal exam ("suprapubic tenderness") and outputs "Incarcerated / strangulated hernia" with "Emergency Theatre: irreducible / strangulated hernia - bowel resection risk" and an emergency laparoscopic inguinal hernia (TAPP) operative plan, for a documented reducible parastomal hernia in a patient with urosepsis.
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts hernia pathway: isIncarcerated must not be set by any "tender" in the abdominal exam; require irreducibility (or tenderness localised to the hernia) and respect "reducible".

guideline.name: NICE NG51 - Suspected sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management
guideline.section: Think sepsis in anyone with a possible infection, including people who are afebrile, older or frail; NEWS2 used for risk stratification in adults in acute hospital settings; high risk -> senior review, blood cultures, lactate and antibiotics within 1 hour
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG51. London: NICE; 2016 (updated 2024).

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening: recommend against qSOFA alone compared with SIRS, NEWS or MEWS; antimicrobials within 1 h for possible septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis; blood cultures before antimicrobials; lactate measurement; 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid within 3 h for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock; noradrenaline first-line vasopressor, MAP target 65 mmHg
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063-e1143.

guideline.name: Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3)
guideline.section: qSOFA: respiratory rate >=22/min, altered mentation, systolic BP <=100 mmHg; >=2 identifies infected patients at risk of poor outcome outside the ICU
guideline.citation: Singer M, Deutschman CS, Seymour CW, et al. JAMA. 2016;315:801-10.

guideline.name: Royal College of Physicians - National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2
guideline.section: Clinical response thresholds: aggregate 5-6 or a single parameter scoring 3 -> urgent response; aggregate >=7 -> emergency response; SpO2 Scale 2 only for confirmed hypercapnic respiratory failure
guideline.citation: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2: standardising the assessment of acute-illness severity in the NHS. London: RCP; 2017.

rationale: Base sepsis case: the afebrile older person. NICE NG51 warns fever may be absent; the web sepsis cascade requires T >=38. NEWS2: RR 24 (2) + SpO₂ 95 (1) + SBP 94 (2) + HR 114 (2) + new confusion (3) + T 36.0 (1) = 11.
